And in the eighth year of Maurice, the Persians rebelled against Hormizd, their king;
and they seized him by treachery,
and blinded his eyes, and he died.
And after ten months,
those who had killed him, because of the multitude of his evil deeds, desired his son Khosrow,
and made him king over them for thirty-eight years.
Bahram, however, a certain Persian general, did not submit to Khosrow,
and rebelled against him insolently with a large army.
Then Khosrow took refuge with the Romans,
and sent secretly to Maurice that he was prepared to come to him,
if he would permit him.
And Maurice, when he heard, rejoiced,
and wrote that he would help him in everything.
And Khosrow set out promptly and came to Edessa.
And John of Sergiopolis received him into his house,
and honoured him greatly.
And he wrote to Maurice
that he would be to him as a servant.
Maurice, however, replied
that he would honour him as a father his son.
And he sent to him John, the commander of the Thracians, with an army of twenty thousand,
and Anastasius, having with him twenty thousand Armenians and Bulgarians.
And he sent forty centenaria of gold for his expenses.
And when Khosrow received these,
he set out for his country.
And Hormuzan the Persian came to him with ten thousand.
The rebels, however, when they heard,
prepared for battle;
and they were defeated and turned their backs.
And the leaders among them were captured and killed,
and the rest turned to Khosrow.
Now that Khosrow gave many gifts to the Romans,
and sent great presents and precious stones to Maurice,
and restored Dara and Resh'aina to the Romans.
And Khosrow asked of Maurice,
and he gave him Maria (Maryam?) his daughter as wife.
And they sent down bishops with her.
And also for his son Theodosius (for the daughter of Theodosius?) he made a very magnificent wedding feast,
and the Patriarch tied the crown.
And Khosrow built three great temples to the Mother of God, and to the Apostles, and to Mor Sergius the martyr;
and the Patriarch of Antioch consecrated them.
And Christianity spread throughout all Persia.
Maurice, however, was puffed up in his mind,
and despised the armies of the Romans,
and did not give them their provisions.
They, however, sent to him:
"God has given peace in your days;
